newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Sime half-year profit within expectations.
newsitem.headline: Sime half-year profit within expectations.

text.p: Malaysian conglomerate Sime Darby Bhd on Saturday reported a 40 percent increase in half-year net earnings, in line with equity analysts' expectations.
Sime said the inclusion of 60 percent-owned Sime Bank for the full half-year results contributed to the higher profits.

The diversified multinational posted a group net profit of 400.0 million ringgit ($161 million) in the six months ended December 31, 1996, against 284.7 million ringgit in the previous corresponding period.
This was achieved on a turnover of 6.38 billion ringgit, compared with 4.78 billion previously.
Pre-tax profit was 784.5 million ringgit, against 502.2 million previously.
The financial services division was the top earner for the group, chalking up a pre-tax profit of 227.2 million ringgit, a tenfold increase from 21.5 million previously.

Analysts had expected strong contribution from Sime Bank, the group's latest jewel. Sime's acquisition of the stake in Sime Bank, Malaysia's fourth largest banking group, was completed in April last year.
Sime's Hong Kong and Singapore operations staged a strong rebound on the back of strong demand for motor vehicles, favourable foreign exchange rates and higher contribution from property sales.
The Hong Kong division reported a pre-tax profit of 74.4 million ringgit, up from 44.6 million previously, while profit from Singapore operations rose to 49.5 million ringgit from 24.8 million.
Sime's Australia operations improved further due to the success of Hastings Deering in several equipment tenders to the mining industry and higher sales to the agricultural sector.
The tractors and property development divisions continued to do well, chalking up profits of 80.4 million and 81.6 million ringgit respectively.
The plantations division, however, saw a decline in profits due to lower crude palm oil prices during the period.
Sime said it expected to maintain the profit level in the second half of the financial year.
According to the Estimate Directory of analysts' forecasts, Sime is expected to announce 817.0 million ringgit in net profits for the year ending June 30, 1997.
